newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares down with last week's Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares down with last week's Wall Street.

text.p: Norwegian shares fell on Monday in moderate trade in reaction to last week's sell-off on Wall Street amid concern about the strong crown, dealers said.
Oslo's Total share index slipped 0.36 percent to close at 1,051.29 points in 690 million crowns of turnover.
"Apart from Wall Street, the appreciating Norwegian crown make some people sell out of concern the strong currency will eventually hit profits for export-oriented companies.
Industrial and banking shares burdened the Total index.

"There was some profit-taking," the dealer said. "Things have gone a bit too fast recently. The upward trend has been liquidity-driven, and it remains to be seen if the companies will produce annual results that exceed expectations."
Saga Petroleum's A share was down 2.7 percent at 124 crowns and industrial group Kvaerner's A share fell 1.3 percent to 304 crowns. Metals maker Elkem fell 2.5 percent to 101 crowns.
The top commercial banks, DnB and Christiania, both fell, but the country's biggest insurance group, Storebrand, rose 1.68 percent to 36.40 crowns.
